::: {.callout-important title="This is a seven-chapter pilot, not the complete workbook"}
This document contains **only Chapters 1 through 7** of *Modern LLM
Architecture: A Visual Guide to Attention, Memory, Sparsity, and Hybrid
Models* (workbook 04 of the ML/LLM Study Workbooks series). Chapter 8
-- a synthesis/practice chapter -- is planned but **not drafted**.
Nothing in this document should be read as implying it exists yet.
Multi-head latent attention (MLA), briefly deferred out of Chapter 3's
drafting pass, is now covered in Chapter 4 alongside sliding-window
and sparse attention. Chapter 4 covers recurrent/state-space/linear-attention
alternatives only as a brief taxonomy and forward reference; Chapter 6
adds the primary source that taxonomy was pending (Gu and Dao's
selective state-space mechanism) once a hybrid case study needed it.
Chapter 5 covers mixture-of-experts architecture only -- detailed
distributed-training implementation, collective-communication
algorithms, kernel optimization, inference-engine configuration,
expert quantization, model-specific benchmark comparisons,
post-training, and routing-research surveys are all deferred to later
workbooks or a future revision. Chapter 6 selects exactly three
real, pinned model families (Llama 3 405B, DeepSeek-V3, Jamba) as
case studies -- it is not a survey of every current model, not a
benchmark ranking, and not a release-history timeline; each model's
architecture facts are dated and traceable to that model's own
technical report, not restated as permanent or "latest" facts.
Chapter 7 synthesizes systems consequences already implied by
Chapters 2-6 (a resource ledger, prefill-vs-decode, an
architecture-to-systems consequence map, and a minimal parallelism
overview); it previews looped depth in one row only (full treatment
deferred to Chapter 8) and cross-references multi-token prediction and
speculative decoding without teaching either mechanism -- both are
assigned to future workbooks in this series' own cross-workbook topic
roadmap, not taught here.

This is a review artifact: it exists to establish the workbook's
explanatory depth, visual language, page density, question style, and
citation style before the remaining chapter is drafted at scale. Treat
any rough edge you find as exactly the kind of thing this pilot is
meant to surface early.
:::
